objections_raised: self-condemnation may be a pointless contradiction
subjective mechanism cannot guarantee objective correctness

appeals_to_authority: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
Religion within the Boundaries of Mere Reason

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: moral accountability, conscience, God as practical postulate

structural_organization.structure_type: thesis-driven with case study and dialectical resolution

summary_of_core_decisions: The text evaluates Kant's account of conscience as the subjective parallel to the categorical imperative, using the Willie case to show that ex post facto conscience is fallible and cannot ground full moral accountability. It argues that God as a practical postulate is necessary to avoid reducing inner self-condemnation to a pointless contradiction, while acknowledging the tension this creates with Kantian autonomy. The conclusion presents Kant's framework as an open invitation rather than a closed system.
